bin_dir.description: Absolute path to the PostgreSQL binary directory containing pg_ctl, psql, etc.

host.description: Host name or IP address of the PostgreSQL server to connect to.

port.description: Port number the PostgreSQL server listens on.

database.description: Database to connect to for checking system catalogs.

username.description: Database user name used for authentication.

auth_method.description: Authentication method to use: trust, password, scram-sha-256, etc. (ensure pg_hba.conf allows it).

password_file.description: Path to .pgpass file for non-interactive password auth. Leave empty to use default locations or prompts.

connect_timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait for a connection before timing out.

check_names.description: List of specific system catalog checks to run. Omit or leave empty to run all standard checks.

verbose.description: If true, output detailed diagnostic information (e.g., queries used).

dry_run.description: If true, simulate the check process without reporting results (mainly for debugging).

skip_types.description: List of object types (e.g., 'toast', 'partition') to skip during checks.

max_errors.description: Stop reporting errors after this many are found. Prevents log flooding.

tolerant.description: If true, always exit with code 0 regardless of issues found (useful for CI pipelines).

check_options.description: Advanced per-check tuning options (if supported by your pg_catcheck version).

check_name.description: Name of the check to configure (e.g., 'index', 'sequence').

description.description: Human-readable description of what this check validates.

enabled.description: Whether this check should be active.

legacy_mode.description: If true, relax validation rules to support older (pre-v12) catalog structures.
